visual_elements.description: Feedforward neural network diagram. Input layer: two circles labeled x1 (top) and x2 (bottom). Arrows to hidden layer: x1->S1 labeled '-1' (red), x1->S2 labeled '1' (blue), x2->S1 labeled '1' (red), x2->S2 labeled '-1' (blue). Hidden layer: two circles labeled S1 and S2 containing sigma (Σ) symbols. From S1 an arrow to a purple-outlined box containing a step-function icon, labeled 'Z1' to its right; above the box are two lines '>0.5 => 1' (yellow) and '<0.5 => 0' (red). From S2 an arrow to a similar box labeled 'Z2'; above it '>= -0.5 => 1' (green) and '< -0.5 => 0' (red). From Z1 an arrow labeled '-1' (red) to output circle S3 (sigma). From Z2 an arrow labeled '1' (green) to S3. From S3 an arrow to a purple-outlined box with step-function icon, labeled 'Z3'/'O/P'; above it '>0 => 1' (yellow) and '<0 => 0' (red). Arrow out labeled 'O/P'.
visual_elements.position: upper-left and center, inside blue-bordered rectangle

recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to light gray (#f2f2f2). 2. Add title text at top: 'Using Two Perceptron Layers with' in red bold sans-serif, then 'non-Linearity' in blue bold sans-serif immediately after. 3. Add a yellow circle with black border at top-right containing '15'. 4. Draw a large blue-bordered rectangle for the neural network diagram on the upper-left/center. Inside, place two input circles x1 (top) and x2 (bottom). Draw weighted arrows to two sigma circles S1 and S2 with labels: x1->S1 '-1' (red), x1->S2 '1' (blue), x2->S1 '1' (red), x2->S2 '-1' (blue). From S1 and S2 draw arrows to purple-outlined step-function boxes labeled Z1 and Z2; above Z1 place '>0.5 => 1' (yellow) and '<0.5 => 0' (red); above Z2 place '>= -0.5 => 1' (green) and '< -0.5 => 0' (red). Draw arrows from Z1 and Z2 to output sigma circle S3 with weights '-1' (red) from Z1 and '1' (green) from Z2. From S3 draw arrow to a final step-function box labeled O/P/Z3 with '>0 => 1' (yellow) and '<0 => 0' (red) above it. 5. To the right of the diagram, create a red-bordered truth table with headers X1, X2, O/P and rows: 0/0/0 (cyan O/P), 0/1/1 (green O/P), 1/0/1 (green O/P), 1/1/0 (cyan O/P). 6. Below the diagram, create a wide red-bordered table with header groups: x2 | x1 || S1 | Z1 || S2 | Z2 || S3 | Z3. Fill rows: 0,0,0,0,0,1,1,1 (last cell cyan); 0,1,-1,0,-1,0,0,0 (last cell green); 1,0,1,1,1,1,0,0 (last cell green); 1,1,0,0,0,1,1,1 (last cell cyan). 7. Add a rounded light-yellow callout box at bottom-right with text: line 1 'Adding Non-Linearity' (blue), line 2 'Solves the' (black), line 3 'XOR Problem' with 'XOR' in red.
